no_plaintext_secretvalue_leakage_in_fano.notes: submitSecretsFanOut() (services/secretsService.js) builds each results[] entry as { environment, success, errorCode, error: error.message } — verified by reading every throw site in submitSecretViaGitOps (7 Error constructors, lines ~545-680) and confirming none interpolates secretValue, only secretName/environment/vaultDir. tests/integration/service/secretsService.spec.ts 'never lets a per-environment error carry a secretValue' asserts JSON.stringify(results) excludes the literal secret value used in the test. The outer route catch block (routes/api.js) was also changed to return a generic 'Failed to submit secrets' message instead of echoing error.message/secretNames/vaults/qualifiers/prUrl as the old single-environment catch did — reduces, not increases, potential leakage surface. routes/api.js's pre-existing redactSecretValues() (recursive, array-aware) is unchanged and still sanitizes express-validator input errors before they're logged.

path_traversal_and_vault_allow_listing.notes: The fan-out loop reuses the unmodified, unchanged submitSecretViaGitOps()/resolveKeyVaults() per environment (services/secretsService.js line ~614-627): vaultDir is validated via `vaults.find(v => v.vaultDir === vaultDir)` against a freshly-resolved, per-(appName,environment,target) vault list on every call — a vaultDir string cannot be reused across environments to reach another environment's or app's vault, because the candidate list itself is scoped to that specific environment/app before the equality check runs. classifyEnvironmentTier() reads a single fixed path (`path.join(__dirname, '../data/environmentTiers.json')`) that is never constructed from request input, so there is no traversal vector through the new tiering code. No new file-path or vault-path construction was introduced by this feature beyond what secret-self-service/secrets-ui-enhancements already hardened.

environmentTiers_json_cannot_bypass_envi.notes: data/environmentTiers.json is read only by classifyEnvironmentTier(), which is purely additive (UI grouping label + audit-log tagging). The express-validator regex gates for `environment`/`environments.*` (`/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,32}$/`, routes/api.js) are unchanged and apply identically regardless of an environment's tier classification or even its absence from the config file. An environment name cannot gain elevated privilege, skip validation, or reach a different vault path by being present/absent in any environmentTiers.json group — the file only ever adds a `tier` label and an audit boolean.

production_confirmation_safeguard_server.result: NOT ENFORCED SERVER-SIDE — CONFIRMED BY DESIGN, NOT A DEFECT
production_confirmation_safeguard_server.notes: Direct answer to the specific question asked: no, POST /api/secrets does NOT reject a request touching a production-tier environment when `confirmedProductionWrite` is false or absent — routes/api.js only uses the field to populate the `secret_create_submitted` audit metric (`confirmedProductionWrite: req.body.confirmedProductionWrite === true`), never as a precondition to proceed. A direct API call (bypassing SecretsPage.vue's modal entirely) can open a production-environment secrets PR without ever having 'confirmed' anything, leaving only `confirmedProductionWrite: false` in the audit log after the fact. This was verified by both static review (routes/api.js lines ~439-489: no early-return/400 branch keyed on confirmedProductionWrite) and an executable test that encodes it as expected behavior: tests/integration/service/secretsFanOutRoute.spec.ts 'logs confirmedProductionWrite:false when a prod-tier environment is submitted without the client claiming confirmation' asserts HTTP 201 (success), not a rejection. This matches the PRD's own resolution of OQ-002 verbatim: 'production writes already flow through a required Jira ticket plus a human-reviewed PR/merge gate downstream, so the portal-level step's job is preventing accidental selection, not serving as the sole control' — i.e. the actual write-enforcement boundary for this feature is the downstream GitHub PR review/merge step (unchanged, unaffected by this client-side-only gate), not the confirmation modal. Classified as a documented, PRD-sanctioned design decision with a compensating control already in place, not a new vulnerability introduced by this diff — but it is a real defense-in-depth gap worth a deliberate stakeholder sign-off, which is why it is called out explicitly here rather than silently accepted. See remediation_plan item 1 if Security/Compliance wants this hardened.

residual_risks: FR-007's production-write confirmation is enforceable only in the UI, not the API (see focus_area_review above) — by explicit PRD design (OQ-002), compensated by the mandatory Jira ticket + human PR review/merge before the write takes effect. Recommend a follow-up decision with Security/Compliance if this compensating control is ever judged insufficient (e.g. if PR auto-merge is introduced for this repo in the future, this gap would become materially more severe and should be revisited immediately at that time).
